question: Why does crash3 fault during Manager registration, and what context must an ordinary reminder retain?
callsite_evidence: crash3: Manager launcher registration completes, then notification event 34/subtype 7 reaches ntf_event_all_cb (0x0c559434), LR 0x0c5595d5.
0x0c55fde8 loads list->head; 0x0c55fdf4 loads message+92 into r5; 0x0c55fe06 executes ldrb r3,[r5,#13]. Crash r5=0 and BFAR=0x0d exactly reproduce this missing-context dereference.

Stock analyze_notify_data/notify_set_user_data (0x0c8ff218) allocates and zeros 16 bytes: phone data +0, focus v1 +4, focus v2 +8, phone active +12, focus version +13. Ordinary messages have message+90=0 and focus version=0.
control_flow_evidence: Reminder start dereferences context+13 unconditionally before any DND/wrist/notification policy branch. Disabling focus does not make user_data optional.
sub_C562518 gates focus-v1/v2 dereferences on message+90. Canopus leaves this zero and supplies no phone/focus callbacks.

sub_C6A6DC8 clones message strings but borrows context+92. sub_C6A6D4C and sub_C8F3FD4 free strings/list nodes, not this context. Two separate writable static contexts live for the boot-resident supervisor lifetime.
ownership_analysis: Each Canopus message borrows its own zeroed 16-byte boot-resident user context; no automatic stack lifetime, no stock phone/focus ownership callback and no freeing of a shared payload.
unsafe_assumptions: Real display/vibration/DND/memory-pressure validation is pending. Emulation covers actual insertion, event consumer and reminder decision code; settings and presentation endpoints are modeled.
recommended_probe: Use the rebuilt exact .139 package after reboot. Register Manager, inspect load notification, dismiss it, install a signed module, inspect/dismiss its notification, and reopen the notification list.
